To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the initial nucleation and the morphology of GaSb grown on GaAs substrates depend on the growth temperature.

(1) the initial nucleation of the GaSb layer on GaAs substrates is a three-dimensional process; (2) the islands experience a transition in morphology as the growth temperature is increased; (3) the transition from elongated islands along the [110 ] to square islands is accompanied by a change in the orientation of stacking faults from the (111) planes to the (001) planes;
the GaSbi/GaAs interface is atomically abrupt and that the islands are coherent and free from defects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of GaSb layers on (001)GaAs substrates by MBE.
the initial stages of growth of GaSb layers on GaAs substrates.
the initial nucleation of III-V compounds grown by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) or metalorganic vapor phase epixtaxy (MOVPE).

the initial growth of GaSb layers on GaAs is governed by the surface diffusion of Ga atoms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the growth temperature is a very important parameter for the morphology and defect structure of GaSb/GaAs islands.
the GaS1-xSbx islands on GaAs are initially formed by a Stranski-Krastanov growth mode.
GaSb islands grown at temperatures above 550°C are nearly defect free and that the growth of the islands is dominated by the surface diffusion of Sb adatoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of the GaSb island is determined by the balance between the surface energy and the interfacial energy between the island and the substrate.

the GaSbi islands grown on GaAs at 560°C are highly defective and have a high density of stacking faults, which may be related to the high growth rate and/or the presence of a high concentration of Sb in the islands.
the GaSbsubstrate interface is not flat and that it is possible to grow high quality GaSb films on (001)GaAs substrates.
